text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: Smart-routing error spike detected for rollout/wn-model-v2 canary in us-west. 5xx ratio > 8% over last 5m, automated fallback to region eu-central triggered. Auto-page to on-call.

alice: ack — I'm on it, grabbing logs and routing table.

alice: quick snapshot — canary was set to 10% traffic, health checks started failing ~10:12 UTC. Router policy kicked in and routed to eu-central variant wn-model-v1-fallback.

mike: pinging — is wn-model-v1-fallback compatible with the canary's response schema? we had a variant switch last week.

alice: looks like the fallback variant returns a shorter completion and sometimes different JSON keys. That mismatch is triggering downstream client errors in some paths.

incident-bot: NOTE: sticky-fallback policy is enabled for this route (policy-id: pf-83a). Requests routed to a fallback will be pinned to that region for session TTL of 10m.

sara: oh right — sticky pin + canary instability => sessions pinned to eu-central while canary continues to receive placement attempts from the control plane. possible routing loop.

alice: reproducing logs from router:
```
2026-03-12T10:12:17Z ROUTER INFO route=generate user=svc-abc ctx=session=se1234 decision=canary->us-west
2026-03-12T10:12:18Z ROUTER WARN route=generate decision=canary-healthy?=false fallback=eu-central sticky_pin=true
2026-03-12T10:12:19Z ROUTER INFO route=generate decision=fallback->eu-central session=se1234
2026-03-12T10:12:20Z ROUTER INFO route=generate decision=route-back->us-west control-plane-assignment=us-west
```

carol: customers flagged: three Dedicated customers reported increased 5xx and timeouts (acct-phi, acct-nova, acct-mero). They're on reserved capacity in us-west but traffic got spilled. I'm drafting incident emails.

dana: i'm next on-call at 10:30 UTC, stand by for handoff.

alice: action plan (short):
- pause canary rollout (control-plane) -> stop new canary assignments
- clear sticky pins for active sessions on affected route
- roll back canary variant to wn-model-v1 for safety if pause doesn't stabilize
- escalate to runtime eng for policy fix (sticky+canary interaction)

mike: +1. I suspect routing policy evaluation order bug: when canary health flips we still have control-plane assignments queued which cause re-assignment attempts, combined with sticky pins means sessions oscillate between regions. I'll take policy fix and a short-term mitigation.

alice: executing step 1: pausing canary now.

incident-bot: COMMAND ACK: canary rollout paused by alice at 10:16 UTC (event id rlt-9921).

alice: executing step 2: running clear sticky for route generate -> issuing admin call.
```
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/routes/generate/clear-sticky" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{"force":true,"reason":"incident 1763501234 - clear pins to break loop"}'
```

incident-bot: CLEAR-STICKY job accepted (job-id cs-558). Running across regions, ETA ~30s.

mike: starting emergency policy patch — change evaluation to prefer stable assignment if fallback sticky exists OR disable sticky on fallback when canary is active. I'll push a config toggle.

sara: customer impact note: affected requests show 12-40s spikes, some timeouts. recommend outage classification: partial degraded (P2) and email to affected accounts.

carol: received confirmations from acct-phi and acct-nova that errors reduced after clear-sticky. acct-mero still seeing issues, I'm opening a dedicated bridge with them.

incident-bot: CLEAR-STICKY job cs-558 completed at 10:17:05 UTC. 98% session pins cleared in us-west/eu-central clusters.

alice: monitoring — error rate dropping to 1.2% now. latency trending down.

mike: policy patch pushed to prod control-plane (toggle: fallback_disable_sticky_during_canary=true). Pushing rollout to 3 control-plane instances.

incident-bot: CONTROL-PLANE: config update applied on instance cp-3 at 10:18:42 UTC.

alice: good signal — no reappearance of loop. Keeping canary paused until further validation.

dana: taking over on-call at 10:30 UTC. I'll own the remediation checklist and follow up with a postmortem draft. alice handing off: current state: canary paused, sticky cleared, policy toggle applied, error rate normalized.

dana: I will coordinate rollback of canary to wn-model-v1 if any regression shows up in next 30m; otherwise we'll schedule a controlled re-run with updated policy.

carol: customer comms sent for acct-phi/acc-nova; acct-mero on bridge. Will update with timeline and mitigation steps.

sara: product note — we need to add a gating test: ensure fallback variant schema compatibility before enabling sticky fallback. Filing ticket P-1421.

mike: root cause hypothesis: control-plane assignment queue + sticky-fallback TTL + incompatible fallback variant -> oscillation. Fix: policy evaluation reorder + safety checks + compatibility verification.

alice: closing actions for now:
- dana to confirm stability and close incident
- mike to land permanent policy change and schema compatibility check (PR and canary)
- sara to add product gating and communicate rollout checklist updates
- carol to finish customer follow-ups

dana: noted, will mark incident as resolved when metrics stable for 45m and customers confirm recovery.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: state=stabilized at 11:05 UTC, incident-id inc-1763501234. Postmortem assigned to dana + mike + sara.

alice: thanks all. we'll draft RCA and include recommended controls: disable sticky on fallbacks during canaries, require variant compatibility checks, and add automated breaker for region-flapping.

carol: adding timeline to ticket and circling back with customers for follow-up meeting. :thumbsup:

dana: handing off full notes to next rotation. leaving oncall ping enabled for 1hr.
